headline: BARMM’s First Parliamentary Vote Moves Into Coalition Phase After High-Turnout Election
seoTitle: BARMM Election Moves Into Coalition Phase After Historic Vote | FMB News
seoDescription: The Bangsamoro region's first regular parliamentary election drew roughly 80% turnout and left no single bloc with an outright majority, pushing the transition into coalition-building.
deck: The Bangsamoro region’s first regular parliamentary election produced strong voter participation but no single bloc with an outright majority, pushing the historic transition from appointed rule into coalition-building.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao entered a new phase of its political transition after voters chose the region’s first regularly elected parliament in the September 14 election.

Reuters reported turnout at roughly 80 percent. No single political bloc emerged with an outright majority in the 80-seat parliament, making coalition negotiations central to the formation of the next regional government.
The result moves BARMM away from years of appointed transitional administration and toward a parliament whose governing majority and chief minister must be produced through the new electoral system.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The election is a major milestone in the peace process that created the Bangsamoro autonomous region after decades of conflict. The parliamentary system combines district seats with party representation and is designed to broaden political participation beyond the structures of the former autonomous region.

The election was not free of disruption. Authorities dealt with violence in parts of Cotabato and Basilan, while the Commission on Elections ordered replacement ballots in Maluso after compromised ballots were discovered. Voting hours were also extended in Al-Barka after security tensions delayed parts of the process.
As canvassing advanced, district winners began receiving official proclamations, but the formation of a governing majority remained dependent on final seat allocation and coalition agreements.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The election is the most important democratic handover yet under the Bangsamoro peace settlement. Its credibility will be judged not only by turnout and results, but by whether competing blocs can form a government without destabilizing the institutions built during the transition.

For communities in BARMM, coalition choices will shape leadership, budgeting, public services and the pace of reforms intended to convert the gains of the peace agreement into functioning regional government.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch final canvassing, party-seat allocation, coalition agreements and the election of the chief minister.
Also watch formal election complaints arising from violence, disrupted voting or compromised ballots, and whether the new parliament can begin work with broad political legitimacy.
